mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows two distinct AuditEntry atoms to share the same Transaction, violating the append-only / no-duplicate invariant. The injection forces exactly such a duplicate to exist.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj ae1, ae2: AuditEntry | ae1.transaction = ae2.transaction }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows a Transaction with source = destination. The injection forces such a self-transfer to exist.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_SelfTransferViolation { some t: Transaction | t.source = t.destination }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows an AccountHolder to initiate a transfer from an account they do not own. The injection forces such a scenario.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OwnershipViolation { some t: Transaction | t.initiator.role = AccountHolder and t.source.owner != t.initiator }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows an Auditor to appear as initiator of a Transaction. The injection forces an auditor-initiated transaction to exist.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditorTransferViolation { some t: Transaction | t.initiator.role = Auditor }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows an AuditEntry to misattribute the initiator or role. The injection forces a misattributed audit entry.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AttributionViolation { some ae: AuditEntry | ae.auditInitiator != ae.transaction.initiator }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows an unauthenticated operation to be permitted. The injection forces an unauthenticated-but-permitted operation.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuthViolation { some o: Operation | o.authStatus = Unauthenticated and o.permitted = True }
